meta.name_placeholder_note: Replace with the user's first name. If no name is set, do not show sentences that contain the placeholder. Show a prompt asking the user to add a name. Never rewrite a sentence.

level_rules.on_feels_true: Show the next level up for this category.
level_rules.on_not_yet: Show the next level down for this category.
level_rules.note: Never show level names to the user. Never label the user as low or high self-esteem.

meta.user_added_sentence_hint: Write something you can believe today.
ui_note_rules: Say 'research found' or 'a study found'. Never say 'proven'.
Use only the claim_ui text. Do not extend it.
Show no note for a category where research_note_id is null.

source_check_key.abstract_read: I read the abstract or study summary.
source_check_key.secondary_only: I saw this only in a news or summary source. Check the primary paper before publishing.

session.note: These numbers are design choices, not tested doses. Do not present them to users as research.

session_modes.say_aloud: Same as standard, but the Read screen asks the user to say the sentence out loud once, just before the event.
session_modes.paper_timer: Read, Check, then a dim five minute timer while the user writes on paper. No sound. No further sentences.

suggest_policies.normal: May be suggested on Today's practice.
suggest_policies.opt_in: Never suggested unless the user has opened this category before.
suggest_policies.limited: Suggested at most once every limited_category_min_days_between_suggestions days.

categories.title: My values
categories.when_to_use: Use when you feel pressure or doubt.

levels.gentle: Some things matter to me more than others, and I can notice what they are.
levels.medium: I know what I value, and I can act on it today.
levels.strong: My values guide my choices, even on hard days.

affirmations.prompt: Name one value. Write one small way you used it this week.

levels.gentle: I do not need to feel confident to act on what I care about.
levels.medium: I can take one small step that fits my values.
levels.strong: I act on what I value, whatever my mood.

affirmations.prompt: Which step fits your values today?

levels.gentle: I can start to notice what does not fit my values.
levels.medium: I can say no to something that does not fit what I value.
levels.strong: I protect my time for what matters to me.

affirmations.prompt: What is one thing you could say no to this week?

categories.title: Kind to myself
categories.when_to_use: Use after a mistake, or when you are being hard on yourself.

levels.gentle: I can try to speak to myself a little more gently today.
levels.medium: I talk to myself the way I would talk to a good friend.
levels.strong: I treat myself with the same kindness I give to others.

affirmations.prompt: What would you say to a friend in your situation? Say it to yourself.

levels.gentle: Making a mistake is part of being human.
levels.medium: This mistake is one event. It is not a verdict on me.
levels.strong: I can learn from this mistake and still respect myself.

affirmations.prompt: Write one thing you can learn from it.

levels.gentle: I can notice when I am being hard on myself.
levels.medium: I can pause and ask what I need right now.
levels.strong: I give myself what I need, as I would for someone I love.

affirmations.prompt: What do you need right now: rest, food, a walk, a call?

categories.title: What my body can do
categories.when_to_use: Use when you are focused on how you look.

levels.gentle: My body did some useful things today.
levels.medium: My body carried me through today, and I can thank it for that.
levels.strong: My body is strong in many ways that have nothing to do with how it looks.

affirmations.prompt: Name three things your body did for you today.

levels.gentle: My hands do many things for me.
levels.medium: My hands cook, write, hold, and comfort. They do real work.
levels.strong: I value my hands for everything they make possible.

affirmations.prompt: Describe one thing your hands did today.

levels.gentle: I can notice one thing my body does well.
levels.medium: My body lets me laugh, walk, rest, and hug people.
levels.strong: I respect my body for what it does every day.

affirmations.prompt: Which of these did you do today?

levels.gentle: Today is hard, and I am still here.
levels.medium: Today is hard, and I am still getting through it.
levels.strong: Today is hard, and I can handle the next hour.

affirmations.prompt: What is the next hour? Write one small step.

levels.gentle: I can feel nervous and still go.
levels.medium: I can feel unsure and still do this.
levels.strong: Feeling nervous does not stop me from acting.

affirmations.prompt: What are you about to do while nervous?

levels.gentle: Some things went badly today. Some things went well.
levels.medium: Both are true: some things went badly, and some things went well.
levels.strong: A bad part of the day does not cancel the good parts.

affirmations.prompt: Write one thing that went badly and one thing that went well.

categories.title: Talking to myself by name
categories.when_to_use: Use when your thoughts keep going round the same worry.

levels.gentle: {name}, what is one small next step?
levels.medium: {name}, you have handled hard moments before.
levels.strong: {name}, you can handle this.

affirmations.prompt: Say it quietly, using your own name.

levels.gentle: {name}, what is going on here?
levels.medium: {name}, why do you feel this way, and what would help?
levels.strong: {name}, you know what to do next.

affirmations.prompt: Answer in one sentence, as if you were advising {name}.

levels.gentle: {name}, what would you tell a friend in this situation?
levels.medium: You are allowed to take your time, {name}.
levels.strong: {name}, you choose how to respond.

affirmations.prompt: Say it quietly, with your name.

categories.title: Before something big
categories.when_to_use: Use right before a speech, meeting, interview, or test.

levels.gentle: My heart is racing. That can also be excitement.
levels.medium: I am excited.
levels.strong: I am excited, and I am ready to begin.

affirmations.prompt: Say it out loud once before you begin.

levels.gentle: Nerves and excitement feel very similar in the body.
levels.medium: This energy can help me perform.
levels.strong: I turn this energy into focus.

affirmations.prompt: Where do you feel the energy? Name the place in your body.

levels.gentle: I can think about how this could go well.
levels.medium: This is a chance to do something that matters to me.
levels.strong: I am looking forward to this chance.

affirmations.prompt: Write one way this could go well.

categories.title: Small good things
categories.when_to_use: Use in the evening. Once or twice a week is enough.

levels.gentle: I can look for one thing that went well today.
levels.medium: One good thing happened today, and I noticed it.
levels.strong: I notice the good things in my day, and I know why they happened.

affirmations.prompt: Write three good things from today and one sentence on why each happened.

levels.gentle: I can think of one person who helped me recently.
levels.medium: Someone made my week easier, and I can thank them.
levels.strong: I tell people when they matter to me.

affirmations.prompt: Who could you thank today? Send one short message.

levels.gentle: A small good moment still counts.
levels.medium: A warm drink, a kind word, a clear sky. Small things count.
levels.strong: I notice small good things, and they matter.

affirmations.prompt: What is one small good thing near you right now?

categories.title: Before sleep
categories.when_to_use: Use before you go to sleep. Write on paper, not on your phone.

levels.gentle: I can write down what is on my mind.
levels.medium: Tomorrow's tasks are written down. They can wait until morning.
levels.strong: My plan for tomorrow exists, so my head can rest.

affirmations.prompt: Write tomorrow's tasks on paper for five minutes. Be specific.

levels.gentle: I do not have to solve everything tonight.
levels.medium: What is unfinished is on paper now, not only in my head.
levels.strong: I decide when to think about this: tomorrow, not tonight.

affirmations.prompt: Which task is first tomorrow morning?

levels.gentle: I can write this worry down instead of holding it in my head.
levels.medium: I can put this worry on paper and look at it tomorrow.
levels.strong: This worry has a first step, and the step is for tomorrow.

affirmations.prompt: Write the worry in one line, then the first step for tomorrow.

categories.title: My future self
categories.when_to_use: Use when you want to look ahead.

levels.gentle: I can imagine a future that goes well.
levels.medium: I can picture my life one year from now, going as well as it can.
levels.strong: I am working toward a future I want.

affirmations.prompt: Write for a few minutes about your best possible life one year from now.

levels.gentle: I can think about one thing I would like to be true next year.
levels.medium: I know one thing I want, and I can take a step toward it.
levels.strong: I move toward what I want with steady steps.

affirmations.prompt: What is one step you could take this week?

levels.gentle: I can wonder what my best year would include.
levels.medium: My best possible future includes things I can start now.
levels.strong: I am building the life I described.

affirmations.prompt: Which part of your best future can start this week?

categories.title: I am not alone
categories.when_to_use: Use when you feel alone with a problem.

levels.gentle: Other women feel this way too.
levels.medium: Many women feel this way. I am not the only one.
levels.strong: My experience is shared by many people, and that connects me to them.

affirmations.prompt: Think of one person who may feel the same. What would you say to her?

levels.gentle: I can ask for help with one small thing.
levels.medium: Asking for help is a normal part of life.
levels.strong: I let people support me, and I support them.

affirmations.prompt: Who could you ask for help this week?

levels.gentle: I belong in more places than I notice.
levels.medium: I belong to groups of people who care about me.
levels.strong: I belong, and I do not have to earn it.

affirmations.prompt: Name one group or person who makes you feel you belong.

categories.title: Midlife and beyond
categories.when_to_use: Use when you want to think about what you value now.
categories.audience: Women aged 46 and older. Show only if the user chooses this category.

levels.gentle: I have learned things that younger me did not know.
levels.medium: My experience is useful to me and to other people.
levels.strong: My experience gives me a clear view of what matters.

affirmations.prompt: Write one thing you know now that you did not know ten years ago.

levels.gentle: I can choose what to spend my energy on.
levels.medium: At this stage of life, I can choose what deserves my time.
levels.strong: I spend my time on what I value.

affirmations.prompt: Name one thing you want more of and one thing you want less of.

levels.gentle: My worth is not decided by my age.
levels.medium: I can value who I am now, not only who I was.
levels.strong: I am a full person at every age.

affirmations.prompt: Describe one thing you are proud of from the past year.

categories.title: Work and voice
categories.when_to_use: Use before a hard task or a conversation at work.

levels.gentle: I can think about why my work matters to me.
levels.medium: Before a hard task, I remember what I value about my work.
levels.strong: I do hard tasks because they matter to me.

affirmations.prompt: Write what you value about this work.

levels.gentle: I can ask for what I need at work.
levels.medium: I can ask clearly for what I need, and a no is not a failure.
levels.strong: I speak up about my work, and my voice counts.

affirmations.prompt: Write the one sentence you want to say.

levels.gentle: I can notice one thing I did well.
levels.medium: What I did well this week is real, and I can say so.
levels.strong: I own my results and I share them clearly.

affirmations.prompt: Name one result from this week, in one sentence.

research_notes.claim_ui: In a lab study, adults who first reflected on their personal values had a lower stress hormone response to a stress test.
research_notes.do_not_say: Do not say it lowers everyday stress or cortisol in daily life.
research_notes.extra_fact: Large replications in schools found mixed and sometimes null results (doi 10.1037/edu0000141). Keep the wording modest.

research_notes.claim_ui: In a study of women, seeing self-compassion quotes led to better mood and body image than seeing neutral images.
research_notes.population: Women viewing images in an experiment
research_notes.source: Reported by the Greater Good Science Center, UC Berkeley. Find the original paper before publishing.
research_notes.extra_fact: A 2015 meta-analysis (Self and Identity, 14(5)) found women score slightly lower on self-compassion than men, with a small difference. Do not present the gap as large.
research_notes.do_not_say: Do not say women lack self-compassion.

research_notes.claim_ui: In a trial with 261 British women aged 18 to 30, writing about what the body can do improved body appreciation, and the effect lasted one month.
research_notes.population: 261 British women, aged 18 to 30, who wanted to improve body image
research_notes.do_not_say: Do not say it works for every age or lasts longer than one month.

research_notes.claim_ui: In experiments, people with low self-esteem felt better when they considered both when a positive statement was true and when it was not, than when they focused only on the positive side.
research_notes.source: Wood, Perunovic and Lee, 2009, Psychological Science 20(7), 860-866
research_notes.do_not_say: Do not say all affirmations are harmful.

research_notes.claim_ui: In experiments, talking to yourself by your own name, instead of using 'I', reduced emotional reactions to negative experiences.
research_notes.source: Orvell et al., 2021, Clinical Psychological Science 9(1), 68-78
research_notes.extra_fact: A 2025 real-life study found the benefit did not appear in every situation.
research_notes.do_not_say: Do not say it always works or that it is effortless.

research_notes.claim_ui: In experiments, people who said 'I am excited' before a speech were rated as more persuasive and competent than people who said 'I am calm'.
research_notes.population: College students and community members, Harvard experiments
research_notes.source: Brooks, 2014, Journal of Experimental Psychology: General 143(3), 1144-1158
research_notes.do_not_say: Do not say it treats anxiety disorders.

research_notes.claim_ui: A large review of gratitude exercises, covering 145 studies and 28 countries, found a small improvement in well-being.
research_notes.source: PNAS, 2025 meta-analysis. Find the original paper before publishing.
research_notes.extra_fact: A separate 2023 review of 25 trials found a small positive effect (g = 0.22). A 2021 review found small effects on depression and anxiety symptoms compared with active controls. In one student study from 2005, counting blessings once a week helped more than doing it three times a week.
research_notes.do_not_say: Do not say it is a strong effect or a treatment for depression or anxiety.

research_notes.claim_ui: In a sleep lab study, young adults who wrote a specific to-do list for five minutes fell asleep faster than those who wrote about what they had already done.
research_notes.population: 57 young adults, one night in a sleep laboratory
research_notes.source: Scullin et al., 2018, Journal of Experimental Psychology: General 147(1), 139-146
research_notes.do_not_say: Do not say it cures insomnia. The sample was small and young. Recommend paper, not a phone.

research_notes.claim_ui: In trials, writing about your best possible future improved mood and positive expectations, mostly for a short time.
research_notes.population: Mostly adult and student samples across many trials
research_notes.source: Carrillo et al., 2019, PLOS ONE 14(9), e0222386 (29 studies). A 2020 review of 34 trials found small effects and no strong follow-up effects.
research_notes.do_not_say: Do not say it creates lasting change.

research_notes.claim_ui: A review of self-affirmation studies found small improvements in well-being, including a sense of community and belonging.
research_notes.population: Teens, college students and adults, across countries
research_notes.source: Zhang et al., 2025, American Psychologist (meta-analysis, 129 tests, 67 studies)
research_notes.do_not_say: Do not say it removes loneliness.

research_notes.claim_ui: In a trial with 140 women aged 46 and older, a short self-affirmation exercise led to higher well-being at follow-up than a control task.
research_notes.do_not_say: Do not describe how long the effect lasts. I did not verify the follow-up length.
